title: The Protective Put Psychological Trap
text: If we have long shares and then we buy that floor, it changes your risk profile a bit. You'll notice that your total upside comes down a little bit. That's because it costs you money to put the hedge on. But then your downside is capped. It's a risk-reward trade-off. You have to remember the relationship between these things. This almost looks like a no-brainer. You almost think, "Well, I should always do this." But what you'll find is very frequently it goes up. The thing goes up. So then you're continually closing these long puts at a loss and you're like, "Damn, I don't really like that." That leads to this scenario for some people where they are comfortable with giving up some of the upside and they still want that defined downside.
